🌍 FM Araghchi describes talks with Russian counterpart as productive

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says talks with his Russian counterpart Sergey Lavrov in Tehran were intensive and productive, focusing on bilateral relations as well as key regional and international developments.

Speaking at a joint press conference in Tehran on Monday following talks with Lavrov, Araghchi described their meeting as very important, intensive, and fruitful talks, saying bilateral relations have taken on new dimensions following the implementation of the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership Treaty.
​
The two sides discussed regional and international developments, as well as practical ways to expand political, cultural and trade relations, Araghchi said, adding that economic cooperation is progressing well.
​
Iran, Russia agree regional issues have no military solution
​
Araghchi noted that Iran and Russia maintain close cooperation and consultations on regional issues and have exchanged views on developments in the Persian Gulf, West Asia, the Caucasus, Europe, the Iran-US negotiations, as well as developments in Ukraine.
​
“Our shared view is that regional issues have no military solution and must be pursued through political means,” the top Iranian diplomat said.
​
“We also discussed insecurity in the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz, which we believe stems directly from the US and Israeli military aggression against Iran, launched on February 28 and continuing in various forms. The imposed war and economic blockade are the main sources of insecurity in the region,” he added.
​
The Iranian foreign minister noted that the two sides have also discussed issues concerning Palestine, Lebanon, and Yemen, stressing that the genocide of the Palestinian people and the Israeli regime’s dangerous expansionism in the region must be stopped.
​
Attacks in Caspian Sea threaten regional security
​
Referring to the review of shared security challenges, Araghchi said that today’s talks included an in-depth discussion of recent security incidents in the Caspian Sea, including attacks on Iranian and Russian commercial vessels and assaults on port infrastructure in the region.
​
“We believe that such activities have serious and direct consequences for regional peace and security, while also causing irreparable damage to the fragile marine environment of the Caspian Sea”, he added.
​
Iran, Russia stress need to de-escalate tensions between Afghanistan, Pakistan
​
Regarding regional issues, particularly those concerning Iran’s eastern neighbors, he stressed that Tehran and Moscow share a common view on developments in Afghanistan, the need to ease tensions between Kabul and Islamabad, and the importance of coordinated efforts to counter terrorist threats.
​
Iran, Russia to counter US unilateralism, strengthen multilateralism
​
Emphasizing the two countries’ shared positions on international affairs, Araghchi said that Tehran and Moscow fundamentally oppose the United States’ aggressive unilateralism and will cooperate within international institutions and forums to strengthen multilateralism and uphold the principles of international law.
​
In this regard, he added, coordination between Tehran and Moscow within key frameworks, including BRICS, the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO), and the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), would continue vigorously.
​

“*The Dark Tower* begins with two people in a desert. It’s the simplest possible opening. There’s nothing in front of the reader to distract them, and King builds the universe from there, one stone at a time.”

Warhammer’s universe spans more than 700 books, but Flanagan doesn’t need to retell all of its lore. He needs to find a story that draws newcomers in without overwhelming them with the scale of the world.

🔊 Defense minister says supplying Armed Forces a priority

📌 Tehran, IRNA - Minister of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics Mehrdad Akhlaghi Ketabchi has vowed that the ministry under his watch will continue to supply the needs of the Iranian Armed Forces.

Akhlaghi made the remarks at a ceremony in Tehran, where he was officially introduced as the new defense minister after securing the Parliament’s vote of confidence.
​
He expressed gratitude for the trust placed in him by senior commanders, the president, and parliamentarians.
​
He also thanked Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, all lawmakers, and Parliament staff for facilitating his vetting and vote of confidence, and praised his colleagues at the Defense Ministry and the Defense Industries Organization, emphasizing the heavy responsibility he carries in continuing to serve the Armed Forces.
​
Stressing the need to accelerate the supply of equipment and items required by the Armed Forces, the defense minister said remaining needs must be pursued and completed more rapidly.
​
Akhlaghi announced that he held his first working meeting at the Defense Ministry after receiving the vote of confidence, saying that given the current circumstances, “not even a one-hour pause” in carrying out duties and pursuing missions is permissible.

Great post by Martin Geddes on trying to live in two different realities & how we bridge them!

I mentioned this last night in our discussion with Robert Craft.  Capt Kyle & I had just talked about this very thing yesterday before the podcast.  I'm sure it's something most of us struggle with.

The exhaustion comes from having to walk in 2 worlds at once.

One is the false matrix: a thick fog of deceit, narrative control, & carefully maintained lies that cloud discernment & keep people trapped in fear & confusion.

The other is the quieter reality we hold by faith and the knowing of what we are actually fighting for. 

It’s the conviction that what lies ahead is the world we were always meant for: Heaven on Earth, stripped of the lies & deception that currently distort everything.

Holding both at the same time is heavy. One demands constant vigilance against the illusion. 

The other requires stubborn faith & knowing that the true design is still unfolding.

Yet that dual awareness is also the point of the journey!

We stay awake in the matrix without becoming of it, while steadily choosing the reality rooted in truth, freedom, and God’s original plan.

The weight is real. 
So is the promise! 👈
